title: Understanding SVD
text: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is a method of decomposing a matrix into three other matrices. It is often used in Principal Component Analysis (PCA).

title: Matrix Dimensions in SVD
text: In SVD, the matrix $X$ is decomposed into $U$, $S$, and $V**T$. What are the dimensions of these matrices?

hintAnswer: U is n by n, S is n by d, V^T is d by d
title: Dimensions of $U$, $S$, and $V**T$
text: Given $X$ is an $n$ by $d$ matrix, what are the dimensions of $U$, $S$, and $V**T$?

title: Rank and Singular Values
text: The rank of a matrix is equal to the number of its non-zero singular values. How does this relate to the rank of $X$?

hintAnswer: There are fewer than $$d$$ non-zero singular values.
title: Non-zero Singular Values
text: If $rank(X)<d$, what can we say about the singular values of $X$?

title: Order of Singular Values
text: Singular values in $S$ are arranged in non-increasing order. What does this imply about the structure of $S$?

hintAnswer: The diagonal of $S$ starts with the largest singular value and decreases or remains the same.
title: Structure of $S$
text: Given that singular values are arranged in non-increasing order, what can we say about the diagonal of $S$?
